title: Efficient Diffusion Models under Nonconvex Equality and Inequality constraints via Landing
claim: Sample quality improves with more trajectory steps then plateaus, and the underdamped variant reaches good quality at much shorter trajectories.
layout: single line plot, four colored series, legend top-right, cross markers on curves
description: A single line chart titled "N vs JSD on S2 Flood". The y-axis is mean JSD distance, running from about 0.10 to 0.16. The x-axis is trajectory length N, and its labels are cropped out of this image. Four colored lines with circular markers are drawn: OLLA in blue, RDDPM (OLLA-P) in orange, ULLA in green and ULLA-P in red. All curves fall steeply at small N. OLLA starts near 0.16 and ULLA near 0.136. The curves then converge to roughly 0.10–0.11 and flatten. At the largest N, ULLA and ULLA-P rise slightly, while OLLA and RDDPM keep falling. Large cross marks sit on the red curve at a small N and on the orange and red curves at a mid-range N. They flag where projection failures stop. A grid and a legend box in the upper right frame the data. The eye goes first to the steep blue drop at the top left.
caption: Mean JSD on S2 flood versus trajectory length N under the fixed T. Cross mark (×) indicates the smallest N values after which projection failures no longer occur during the forward process.
abstract: Generative modeling within constrained sets is essential for scientific and engineering applications involving physical, geometric, or safety requirements (e.g., molecular generation, robotics). We present a unified framework for constrained diffusion models on generic nonconvex feasible sets $Î£$ that simultaneously enforces equality and inequality constraints throughout the diffusion process. Our framework incorporates both overdamped and underdamped dynamics for forward and backward sampling. A key algorithmic innovation is a computationally efficient landing mechanism that replaces costly and often ill-defined projections onto $Î£$, ensuring feasibility without iterative Newton solves or projection failures. By leveraging underdamped dynamics, we accelerate mixing toward the prior distribution, effectively alleviating the high simulation costs typically associated with constrained diffusion. Empirically, this approach reduces function evaluations and memory usage during both training and inference while preserving sample quality. On benchmarks featuring equality and mixed constraints, our method achieves comparable sample quality to state-of-the-art baselines while significantly reducing computational cost, providing a practical and scalable solution for diffusion on nonconvex feasible sets.
